projects.name: Empowering and nurturing leadership skills of youth through climate action education in Uzbekistan
projects.description:
This three-year joint initiative by UNDP, the “Education Above All” Foundation (EAA-Qatar), and Ministry of Pre-school and School Education of the Republic of Uzbekistan aims to equip 1.3 mln school students and youth across the Republic of Karakalpakstan, Bukhara, Navoiy, Khorezm, Samarkand, Kashkadarya and Surkhandarya regions with climate knowledge, leadership capacities and “green” skills.

By integrating climate change education into the formal school curriculum and training 50,000 teachers, the project ensures that every student gains access to interactive learning tools. This will help students explore key climate change topics, build understanding of climate science, adaptation and mitigation strategies, environmental sustainability, and practical actions individuals and communities can take to address climate crisis.   

Concurrently, the project establishes a network of 800 Young Green Ambassadors who, together with other youth in their communities, co-design and implement 48 community-led climate actions —ranging from planting drought-resilient species in Moynak to launching sustainable aquaculture initiatives.  

Finally, in partnership with 12 vocational training centers, the project offers two specialized courses to 4,000 young people – one on renewable energy and the other on climate-smart agriculture. These courses help improve job prospects while promoting low-carbon livelihoods. The project also emphasizes gender balance, with at least 48%women participation, and uses digital tools to enhance learning.  Overall, the project supports Uzbekistan’s commitments under the Paris Agreement, the National Green Economy Strategy, and contributes to global goals on quality education, clean energy, decent work, and climate action (SDGs 4, 7, 8 and 13).

The project aims to establish a centralized Situational and Data Analytics Centre combining expertise in geodata analysis, drone technology and satellite imagery. The Centre will generate high-quality data on soil composition and other environmental parameters to support regional policymakers with evidence-based insights. By building a robust technological infrastructure for real-time monitoring and data-driven decision-making, the project will strengthen national capacities in data analytics, geospatial intelligence, remote sensing and smart ecosystem management.
The project will contribute to a knowledge-based economy by creating capacity-building opportunities, driving local technological innovation and generating new business prospects, particularly in smart agro-processing and manufacturing. The integration of digital tools will not only enhance ecosystem restoration but also support sustainable economic and industrial development in the region.

projects.name: Implementation of the Biosafety Mechanism in Uzbekistan in accordance with the Cartagena Protocol
projects.description:
The export-oriented and industrialization centered agricultural strategy of Uzbekistan favors a limited number of standard and uniform varieties of fruits and vegetables. Along with threats posed by climate change and land degradation, it puts traditional local varieties at risk of disappearance. While gaps in the identification and monitoring of the components of agrobiodiversity used on-farm limit their potential for conservation and sustainable use. Altogether, this threatens national food sovereignty, food security and rural livelihood and disrupts the climate change adaptation potential the diversity of local varieties represents.

Following the same chain of thought, it is essential for the country to implement the Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety at the national level. The Cartagena protocol aims to protect biological diversity from the potential risks posed by living-modified organisms (LMOs) resulting from modern biotechnology. The potential risks include transgene flow to wild relatives, loss of genetic diversity, invasiveness, changes in agricultural practice that may be unsustainable, and changes in ecosystem landscape and functions, among others, the preservation and maintenance of local and wild varieties not only important nationally but also globally.

projects.name: PHC-integrated immunisation quality and safety system institutionalised nationwide
projects.description:
Immunisation is delivered as a standardised, safe, people-centred PHC service with routine quality improvement, strong cold-chain integrity, and functional vaccine safety (AEFI) governance—embedded in PHC management and accountability arrangements.
Institutionalised supportive supervision as a PHC quality cycle: Convert the 2024–2025 large-scale supervision model into an annual national cycle with: (i) minimum coverage thresholds for facilities/vaccination points; (ii) corrective action tracking facility → district → region; (iii) supportive mentorship competency standards; Integrate supervision outputs into district PHC performance reviews (not parallel reporting); 
Cold-chain and vaccine management assurance (routine, not campaign-only):- Standard operating standards for storage, temperature monitoring, stock management, open-vial policy, and waste management, aligned with updated national norms and operational guidance; Expand use of remote temperature monitoring as a management tool (exception reporting, response times, accountability). 
Vaccine safety/AEFI governance fully operational: Implement the sequenced reform package identified through the 2024 system assessment: clarified roles, standardised case definitions/classification, causality assessment procedures, single reporting pathway and database, routine performance indicators, and tested crisis communication SOPs; Ensure alignment with WHO global vaccine safety strategic directions.
projects.outcome: Strengthened capacities of the health system to deliver quality, people-centered services across the life course at all levels, aligned with the primary healthcare approach.

projects.name: “Data for action” immunisation system strengthened for equity, life-course coverage, and outbreak resilience
projects.description:
A coherent immunisation intelligence approach is used at PHC and district levels to identify missed populations, reduce drop-outs, and sustain high coverage, supported by fit-for-purpose digital systems and people-centred community engagement.
EIR governance and interoperability for management use (not only reporting): Establish and enforce data quality rules (unique identity and deduplication, denominator coherence, completeness and timeliness), with routine dashboard review mandated in district management cycles; Progress interoperability with core national digital systems where feasible (PHC registers and civil registration/ID services), ensuring privacy and role-based access.
Equity-oriented microplanning institutionalized: Institutionalise micro-mapping and targeted planning as routine PHC practice: ‘who is missed, where, and why’ translated into outreach plans, defaulter tracing, and supervision follow-up; Apply lessons from documented antigen gaps (e.g., availability constraints and missed opportunities) to strengthen service integration and counselling at PHC points.
Integrated VPD risk signals for sustained measles and rubella control: Implement elimination-standard measles and rubella surveillance improvements (case classification, laboratory linkages, and CRS surveillance description and reporting) in line with RVC feedback and WHO/Europe guidance; Use EIR and surveillance outputs jointly for risk-based targeting through district dashboards integrating coverage, drop-out, and outbreak signals.
People-centred demand and confidence (behavioural insights to scalable tools): Translate behavioural insights work (e.g., COM-B-informed analyses) into PHC-ready counselling aids, refusal follow-up scripts, and targeted community engagement packages.
projects.outcome: Strengthened capacities of the health system to deliver quality, people-centered services across the life course at all levels, aligned with the primary healthcare approach.

projects.description:
The project aims to contribute to building a more resilient, inclusive and informed society in Uzbekistan by enabling citizens to exercise their rights to access public information and by strengthening the rule of law and better journalism education. It also aims at enhancing media and information literacy. From three different perspectives, namely freedom of expression and access to information, media development, and media & information literacy, the project addresses the importance of freedom of expression and information as a pubic good and a vital element of democratic governance that contributes to citizen empowerment and collective action. A resilient information society requires three elements: a) empowered citizens who can demand and manage relevant information, b) robust and independent media that can produce quality content, and institutions guided by the rule of law that uphold freedom of expression as a human right, and c) a strategy to embed media and information literacy into the social and educational fabric of the country, involving educators, parents, children, and policymakers alike. 
(Project title: "Empowering the Government and Citizens of Uzbekistan by Strengthening Access to Information, Accountability of Institutions and Media Competence")

projects.name: Regional analysis and evidence for migration policy to improve the effectiveness of humanitarian and development efforts on migration and human mobility, collect and analyze information on human mobility in, to and from the country, and to contribute to evidence-based humanitarian and development programming in Uzbekistan.
projects.description:
Regional Evidence for Migration Analysis and Policy (REMAP) project was developed in response to the critical need to collect and analyze information on (protracted) displacement and human mobility in, to and from Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Pakistan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan and to contribute to evidence-based humanitarian and development programming in these countries and in the region. The data collected will serve as a foundation for determining the numbers, locations, vulnerabilities, and basic needs of diverse mobile populations, which encompass internal and international migrants, Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs), returnees, and host communities within the target countries. This information will be invaluable for informing future humanitarian and development planning and policy. 

REMAP’s overall objective is to improve the effectiveness of humanitarian and development efforts on migration and displacement in Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Pakistan, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan. To achieve this, it harnesses the Displacement/ Mobility Tracking Matrix (DTM/MTM) developed by the International Organization for Migration (IOM), a proven system that has been successfully employed in more than 121 countries since 2004 for tracking and monitoring displacement and population mobility. By deploying the MTM as its primary data collection methodology, the current project strives to advance the comprehension of displacement, migration, and return dynamics in the target countries. Furthermore, it seeks to promote regional interoperability and harmonization of displacement, and population mobility data collection initiatives as well as improve the generation, utilization, and management of such data.
